title: Euclidean Geometry: Circle Theorems
seo_title: Grade 11 Circle Theorems Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Investigate and prove the theorems of the geometry of circles: the line from the centre perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord; the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle at the circumference; angles in the same segment are equal; opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary; two tangents from a point are equal; the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 11 circle geometry worksheets: chords, the angle at the centre, angles in a semicircle and the same segment, cyclic quadrilaterals and tangents. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Angle at the centre = 2 × angle at the circumference.
key_sub: Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles add to 180°.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The line from the centre perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord.
  • The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. The angle in a semicircle is 90°.
  • Angles in the same segment are equal. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°.
  • A tangent is perpendicular to the radius. The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment.

Examples

Example

Angle at the circumference = 35°

angle at the centre = 2 × 35°

Answer: 70°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
HalvingThe centre angle is double.
Equal opposite anglesThey add up to 180°.
The tangentTangent ⊥ radius: 90°.

items.q: O is the centre of the circle. OM is perpendicular to the chord AB, OM = 12 cm and the radius is 13 cm. Find the length of AB.
items.e: OM bisects AB. MB = √(13² − 12²) = √25 = 5 cm, so AB = 2 × 5 = 10 cm.

items.e: OM bisects AB. MB = √(34² − 30²) = √256 = 16 cm, so AB = 2 × 16 = 32 cm.

items.e: M is the midpoint, so MB = 8 cm. OM = √(17² − 8²) = 15 cm.

items.e: P is on the minor arc, so use the reflex angle at the centre: 360° − 76° = 284°. ∠APB = 284° ÷ 2 = 142°.

items.q: AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O. ∠CAB = 49°. Find ∠ABC.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O. The radius is 15 cm and OT = 17 cm. Find the length of TA.
items.e: ∠OAT = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius). TA = √(17² − 15²) = 8 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from the point T to a circle. TA = 8 cm. What is TB?
items.e: Tangents from an external point are equal in length: TB = 8 cm.

items.q: TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. OA = 24 cm and TA = 10 cm. Find OT.
TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O, and ∠ATB = 70°. Find ∠TAB.
items.e: TA = TB, so △TAB is isosceles: ∠TAB = (180° − 70°) ÷ 2 = 55°.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from the point T to a circle. TA = 9 cm. What is TB?
items.e: Tangents from an external point are equal in length: TB = 9 cm.

items.q: TA is a tangent to the circle with centre O. OA = 6 cm and TA = 8 cm. Find OT.
TA and TB are tangents from the point T to a circle. TA = 16 cm. What is TB?

items.q: TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O. The radius is 6 cm and OT = 10 cm. Find the length of TA.
items.e: ∠OAT = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius). TA = √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O, and ∠ATB = 90°. Find ∠OTA.
items.e: OT bisects the angle between the tangents: ∠OTA = 90° ÷ 2 = 45°.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents to the circle with centre O. The radius is 20 cm and OT = 29 cm. Find the length of TA.
items.e: ∠OAT = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius). TA = √(29² − 20²) = 21 cm.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 12 and OP = 20. Find PA.
items.e: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so △OAP is a right triangle with hypotenuse OP. PA = √(20² − 12²) = 16.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 20 and OP = 29. Find PA.
items.e: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so △OAP is a right triangle with hypotenuse OP. PA = √(29² − 20²) = 21.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 9 and PA = 12. Find OP.
items.e: OA ⟂ PA, so OP is the hypotenuse: √(9² + 12²) = 15.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 7 and OP = 25. Find PA.
items.e: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so △OAP is a right triangle with hypotenuse OP. PA = √(25² − 7²) = 24.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 5 and OP = 13. Find PA.
items.e: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so △OAP is a right triangle with hypotenuse OP. PA = √(13² − 5²) = 12.

O is the centre of the circle. ∠AOB = 116°. Find ∠OAB.
items.e: OA = OB (radii), so △OAB is isosceles: ∠OAB = (180° − 116°) ÷ 2 = 32°.

O is the centre of the circle and ∠APB = 34°. Find ∠OBA.
items.e: ∠AOB = 2 × 34° = 68° (angle at centre). OA = OB, so ∠OBA = (180° − 68°) ÷ 2 = 56°.

items.q: O is the centre of the circle and ∠APB = 40°. Find ∠OBA.
items.e: ∠AOB = 2 × 40° = 80° (angle at centre). OA = OB, so ∠OBA = (180° − 80°) ÷ 2 = 50°.
